ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, O, and B are on the same horizontal straight line, and O is located on line AB; a ray OC is drawn from point O, with the direction toward the upper left. Ray OC divides the straight angle AOB into two adjacent angles: ∠AOC and ∠BOC. Reasoning: Because OA and OB are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠AOC and ∠BOC form a pair of adjacent supplementary angles, and the sum of their measures is 180°. It is known that ∠AOC = 53°17', so ∠BOC = 180°00' - 53°17'. Since the minutes are not enough to subtract, borrow 1° = 60', obtaining 180°00' = 179°60', therefore ∠BOC = 179°60' - 53°17' = 126°43'.

Compute ∠BOC = 180°00' − 53°17'. Borrow 1 degree as 60 minutes: 179°60' − 53°17' = 126°43'.
